## Comparison with builtin `grDevices::chull`
Each sample is of the size of `100 000 000` points.

`rcauchy`, `runif`, `rnorm` – numbers drawn from the Cauchy, uniform and normal distribution.

"Segment": all points are collinear and located on the `(0, 0) – (1, 1)` segment.

Tested on: Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSC, Intel Core i7-14700HX @ 2.304 GHz (20c/28t).

Exact code used for `geometria`: `C.chull(x, y, "quick", "indices")` (the Quickhull algorithm).

```{r echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)
results <- data.frame(
  Rozkład = c("rcauchy", "runif", "rnorm", "segment"),
  geometria = c(1.405, 1.882, 1.492, 1.241),
  base_chull = c(2.291, 2.819, 2.277, 1.505)
)
```

```{r echo=FALSE}
barplot(rbind(results$geometria, results$base_chull),
        beside=TRUE, names.arg=results$Rozkład,
        legend.text=c("geometria", "grDevices::chull"),
        ylab="czas [s]", main="n = 1e8")
```
